title: the birth of the cousins
hook: King Pandu, out hunting, shoots a deer that turns out to be a sage, and the dying sage's curse shuts the door on his sons

segments.voice: Yesterday in the birth of the cousins: the crown went to Pandu, and Gandhari bound her eyes. What did you share with someone close? Day seven hundred twenty-five.

A stag and a doe, together in a quiet forest clearing. A king on the hunt sees them through the trees, draws his bow, and shoots, quickly, without a word of warning. The arrows strike the stag, and it falls. And then, lying in the grass, it speaks, in a man's voice. King Pandu has just shot a sage. What the dying stag says next will shape the cousins' story.
screen: `A STAG AND A DOE.` → `THE ARROWS STRIKE.` → `THE DEER SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Back up a little. Pandu has had a good reign. At her self-choice, the princess Kunti, adopted daughter of King Kuntibhoja, chose him for her husband. Bhishma also brought him a second wife, Madri, sister of the king of the Madras. Pandu rode out and won wars, and filled the treasury. Then he went to live in the forest, with both his wives, and spent his days hunting. That's where he meets the deer. The stag is a sage named Kindama, who had taken a deer's form to be with his wife. And as he dies, he says: even a king who hunts should not strike creatures in a moment like this. You've killed me in a moment of love. So hear this. When you go to your wife in love, you will die. And he dies. Pandu is undone. He grieves for the sage, and for himself. He's a king with no son, and now he can never father one. So he makes a decision: he'll give up the throne's life entirely, and live as an ascetic, begging, fasting, with no home. He gives away his jewels and royal robes to Brahmanas, and sends his attendants back to Hastinapura with the news. Kunti and Madri refuse to go back. They say they'll practice austerities beside him. Notice the turn. Yesterday, the crown went to Pandu and passed over his blind brother. Today, the crowned king sits in a forest, unable to have heirs, while back in the palace, Dhritarashtra and Gandhari remain. The story has quietly tipped. And Pandu, looking at his empty future, begins to ask how the line can go on without him.
screen: `KUNTI AND MADRI.` · `A KING GOES TO THE FOREST.` · `KINDAMA'S CURSE.` · `A KING WITH NO HEIRS.`

segments.voice: Let the body settle and the breath lengthen. Pandu's arrow left the bow in an instant, and the curse lasted the rest of his life. Bring to mind a quick action of yours that had long consequences, good or hard: a word, a click, a choice. Don't judge it. Just trace it, the way you'd follow a river from its source. Breathe in at the moment it began. Breathe out along everything that followed. Then rest in the breath alone. The bell holds the time.
The birth of the cousins. A king's arrow, a sage's curse, and a crowned man with no way to have sons.
screen: `THE BIRTH OF THE COUSINS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the birth of the cousins. Today, before one quick action, pause long enough to ask what it might set going. Day seven hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Ahimsa, not harming living beings, is an important value in Hindu traditions, and stories like Kindama's are retold to show how seriously a harm, even in a lawful hunt, can be taken.

pairs: the sage in a deer's form
death if he goes to his wife in love

myth: Pandu knew the deer was a sage
the stag spoke only after the arrows struck.
they refused, and stayed in the forest beside him.
after the curse Pandu chose to live as an ascetic
he gave up the royal life, gave his jewels away, and sent his attendants home.

fork.setup: you're Pandu. a sage's curse means you can never father a son. what do you do?
options: return to the palace and rule.
give up the royal life and live as an ascetic.
fork.reveal: he becomes an ascetic in the forest, and Kunti and Madri insist on staying with him.

original.note: Sanskrit shapa: a curse, like the one the sage Kindama speaks as he dies.

trapdoor: what you thought: a hunting accident.
what it means: a king's careless arrow that takes away his own future.
what a scholar hears: the curse leaves the crowned brother without heirs, while the passed-over brother remains in the palace.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Kunti's self-choice; Madri; Pandu's conquests and retreat to the forest; the sage Kindama's curse; Pandu's resolve)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Kunti chooses Pandu at her swayamvara; Bhishma obtains Madri from Shalya, king of the Madras; Pandu's conquests; his retreat to the forest with both wives; Kindama in deer form; the wording of the curse; Pandu sending his ornaments to Hastinapura; Kunti and Madri refusing to return.
Kunti's earlier boon from Durvasa and the birth of Karna are deliberately held for 'Karna's abandonment' (days 728–733) and day 726.
The curse is phrased gently for a general audience; confirm it remains faithful.
howItsDone makes a general statement about ahimsa; confirm phrasing.
